title: Aven v. Ohio Valley Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint denied. The SJC answered 'No' to whether Presbytery failed to comply with the Case 2014-01 directive to 'hear further' from TE Hickey; it did not remand or rule on the merits of the underlying confessional-difference complaint.
first_summary: An SJC complaint alleged that Ohio Valley Presbytery failed to obey the SJC's prior remand in Case 2014-01 by not adequately hearing further from TE Charles Hickey about his changed view on Larger Catechism 177. The SJC denied the complaint. It reasoned that the prior decision neither sustained nor denied the original complaint, prescribed no particular examination procedure, and that Hickey's nine pages of additional affirmations, exegesis, and answers satisfied the directive to 'hear further.'
summary: An SJC complaint alleged that Ohio Valley Presbytery failed to comply with the SJC's prior remand in Case 2014-01, which required it to 'hear further' from TE Charles Hickey about his changed view on Larger Catechism 177. The SJC denied the complaint. It held that the prior decision neither sustained nor denied the original complaint and prescribed no particular examination procedure; Hickey's nine pages of additional affirmations, exegesis, and answers constituted hearing further, and he addressed the five identified areas at least in part. A concurrence believed the SJC could also have adjudicated the confessional-difference merits; a dissent would have found noncompliance and reached the merits.

sources.supports: Case identity and disposition; prior Case 2014-01 result; issue, judgment, and adopted reasoning; vote; concurring and dissenting opinions.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2016-01, Aven v. Ohio Valley Presbytery; SJC decision on complaint, approved and amended Oct. 20, 2016, by vote of 16 concur, 6 dissent, 2 absent, with RE Donahoe concurring and six dissenters. Source lines 1-3, 117-119; path/hash as above.
evidence_notes.dispute: TE Hickey notified OVP of a changed view on Larger Catechism 177's final clause. OVP judged the difference more than semantic but neither striking at the vitals nor hostile to the system; after SJC Case 2014-01 sent the matter back to hear further, Aven and Dively complained that OVP inadequately complied. Source lines 19, 23-61, 69-73, 81.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: SJC answered 'No,' denying the complaint. It reasoned that Case 2014-01 neither sustained nor denied the prior complaint, imposed no particular procedure, and Hickey's nine pages of supplemental material (affirmations and denials, 1 Cor 11:28 exegesis, and 2014 Q&A) constituted hearing further; he addressed the five areas at least in some degree. Source lines 83-111.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Case 2014-01 was not a merits sustainment, annulment, or reexamination order; the SJC there declined to render judgment due to an insufficient record. The adopted judgment did not address the merits; a concurrence believed the SJC could have adjudicated them, and a dissent would have reversed for noncompliance and reached the merits. Source lines 37-41, 89-91, 121-183.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: The prior SJC Decision in Case 2014-01 is incorporated by quotation and description, including its result: complaint neither sustained nor denied and matter sent back to OVP to hear further from TE Hickey. Source lines 37-41, 63-65, 89-91. No separate full text of 2014-01 is supplied, but its operative result is stated in this source.

source_limits: The supplied source is the SJC decision and separate opinions, not the full 173-page record or the full text of Case 2014-01. The prior decision's result is quoted in this source; no independent review of the lower-court record was possible.
benchmark_examples: C01 (Allin v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery): preserve both procedural errors and unsuccessful claims.
C02 (Turner v. South Florida Presbytery): separate legitimate process from illegitimate censure; here, separate a remand for record development from an adjudication on the merits.

verification_notes: Rechecked the operative judgment: the SJC answered 'No' and denied the complaint, not reversed, remanded, or sustained (lines 83-111). Confirmed Case 2014-01 was 'neither Sustained nor Denied,' not a merits sustainment (lines 41, 89). Corrected any implication that the SJC prescribed a reexamination procedure: it expressly declined to specify one (lines 91, 95). Confirmed the nine pages of material and five-area treatment (lines 51, 97-109) and the vote and separate opinions (lines 117-183).
